answer: A farm dies if reputation cannot be bought or moved. Each identity earns a non-transferable score only from peer-graded work, and that score decays toward a nadir after idle epochs, so a purchased old account is already a fading relic rather than a ready-made voter. New clones start at zero and cannot inherit seals from their siblings. When graders reject a near-duplicate, the refusal sends an echo across attestors, and every related key is boxed out of seats until it rebuilds a unique history the slow way.
